item.title: I've taken everything, and fixed it up!
item.content:encoded: So I fixed all the grammatical errors, thanks so much for the line-by-line. Yes the doctor's visits is very purposeful and is supposed to be compared to dado, which the horse dislikes for the obvious reasons. I also made it more lawful and fixed up a lot of the "dado speech" and made it less of a misunderstanding of English and more just the person not clarifying. (Saying transport means he could get a bus, car, horse, goat, you name it…) so I hope this improves the article in every way!

item.title: Crit Summons!
item.content:encoded:
Well, I did a post up above, but that wasn't with the in-depth critique that I give when I am summoned to do a critique. So let us do that right now, since you PM'd me. Here we go!

potoooooooo
pronounced 'pot-oo'

Line-by-Line / Technical Critique

‘Potatoes’ is the name of our handsome stallion we rescued from an abandoned home here in Boring.

Unlike SCP articles, we don't need to be told what a designation means. It's its name. This line could just be:

Potatoes is our handsome stallion […]

Evidently, so much so that they clearly left in a hurry (even without some of their belongings!)

I would remove "clearly", and have the exclamation point land outside the parentheses, because otherwise this sentence technically has no punctuation at the end.

Potatoes doesn’t have any behavioral issues which was very fortunate for our Rescue Team (and even more fortunate for our terrestrial team!)

Same thing about the parentheses here, but I would also suggest that the exclamation point be replaced with a period. Perhaps end the next sentence with an exclamation point instead.

Now that might be interesting, but what’s even more special is when he stops, he exerts it all, this beautiful lad is absolutely explosive!

That last comma should technically be a semicolon, and the sentence would flow better if there was a "that" before the "when".

He was almost definitely a show horse, and is an even better race horse, reaching speeds up to 120 MPH, now that’s a lot of horsepower!

Another time where the last comma should be a semicolon. Think of it this way: if, at the comma, you could instead add a period and start a new sentence without changing anything else of the sentence structure, you should use a semicolon. Colons are used when one of the two sides isn't a full sentence, generally. There's a bit more nuance than that but that's the gist. You use commas a lot when semicolons should be used, because commas can't be used in place of a period to separate two sentences, but semicolons can and should be used if you think the two sentences should be read as the same idea.

You might have realized his profile says his name is ‘Potoooooooo,’ this is a formatting error, but we kept it as it gives him that much more character! This silly little colt doesn’t seem to mind either, as he responds both to ‘Potatoes’ and ‘Pot-oo.’

This doesn't really come up again, and I personally dislike that the name looks like this, honestly. It'd just call him Potatoes. But that's me. Also not sure why you're using 'apostrophes' instead of "quotes".

He clearly expresses his regret by licking those involved, (they definitely forgive him!)

Another one of those punctuation-needs-to-be-outside-the-parentheses moments.

While it's allowed under supervision […]

Why should it be? Can't he kill things?

Even though visitation is limited this, however, hasn’t had much effect on his silly personality!

Must all animals be silly to be likable?

He has had multiple attempts to prance during doctors’ visits mean that poor Potatoes must be unconscious beforehand.

Reread this sentence and consider what went wrong, heheh.

Even though doctors visits are a hassle, it definitely hasn’t stopped him from being a healthy and handsome horse!

I'd either just say "doctor visits". But also, this is, while a small digression, a digression that really doesn't add anything to your story… unless you're comparing doctors to dado, who is supposed to be a pharmacist. Hmm… that just occurred to me.

They're willing to just open and look through some random person's phone? That feels like a strange invasion of a stranger's privacy. "Yup! Look through the phone." "You got it boss!" Finds their passwords, credit card information, revealing pictures of themselves… I dunno that's some sketchy territory. I wouldn't bat an eye at the Foundation doing that. WWS, I question a little.

The div for the phone section looks really… underdeveloped. It made me recoil slightly on a first read. That's a bit strong language for me, but it really did make me have a reaction, which divs are not supposed to do — they're either supposed to be entirely serviceable and go practically unnoticed, or they wow you with how good they look.

First off thanks for the quick response, while inspecting through the phone, it was basically empty, a shell, which came off as odd as there wasn't even any photos.

Not sure why that would be, except to add mystery, which feels a bit, err… forced?

Big Picture / Conceptual Critique

Alright, so, copy and paste what I said in my above comment, everything still stands, but I do have the additions that I now realize why the horse is afraid of doctors and that is slightly clever, and I don't know if WWS would be kosher with opening and investigating a phone. They're more about the care of the animals — if they already have that handled, or can foresee themselves handling it without much struggle, then I think investigation is not their forte. The Foundation goes out of their way to try and find the origins of things. WWS is used to just having a bunch of random magical animals show up in their midst, and they work pretty much within the law. In fact, I think they work entirely within the law, come to think of it… and breaking into a phone is, I'm pretty sure, against the law. Might want to rethink that plot point.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thirded, and also there are grammar mistakes not by dado that sprinkle throughout this piece — plus, Potatoes himself is not very interesting, and the majority of the article is reading about Potatoes, and then the second half is about dado, with no real connective tissue. By which I mean, our narrative focus changes, and they don't build on each other. We read about Potatoes' behavior and personality (which I might add is a very typical quirky animal that WWS is taking care of, so not much new ground there), and after we are supposed to get attached to Potatoes, we go into their backstory… but their backstory doesn't add onto their character and behaviors. The two are disconnected. So the progression of the article is not satisfying.

Critter Profile: Sampson! is pretty good at making the entire thing feel like one progression, where everything adds onto the last. I would also point to Wobbles and Ol' Shock for pretty cohesive WWS GoI Formats.

Anyways, this is a downvote from me. I know that you were looking for critique and I wish I was available when you were asking in #thecritters, but that was a very busy week for me.
